description: Na₂FeO₄ crystallizes in the triclinic P̅1 space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.59 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted NaO₅ square pyramids that share corners with three equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, edges with two equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.47 Å. Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids and  an edgeedge with one NaO₅ square pyramid. There are two shorter (1.65 Å) and two longer (1.67 Å) Fe-O bond lengths. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one Fe atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to two equivalent Na and one Fe atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one Fe atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to two Na and one Fe atom.
